title: CLO Tips Classroom - Automatic Dressing Tool
description: CLO technical experts teach you how to quickly complete automatic fitting of different sizes (including external models) in minutes.
transcript:
Today we will learn how to use the Automatic Clothing Tool.  
For example, when the model is the default model of CLO,  
when the costume is completed,  
and the model size needs to be adjusted or the pose is made,  
how to automatically dress the 3D costume on the virtual model?  
This is a file with code information.  
Click on the 3D model in the object window to match the 3D model.  
Select the model of the corresponding size in the folder.  
Click on the Automatic Clothing Tool in the 3D toolbar.  
You can see that the costume is completed very quickly according to the model size.  
The remaining two poses are operated the same way.  
Change the size of the object window and match the 3D shape.  
Click on the Automatic Clothing Tool in the 3D toolbar.  
In this way, you can quickly complete the costume fitting corresponding to the size.  
Next is the last size.  
It is the same as the previous operation.  
In this way, you can quickly complete the production of this pose file.  
In the menu bar, find Production and select Check Pose.  
Now you can see the fitting effect of each size on one page.  

Example 2. When you need to use an external model,  
the external model cannot use the Automatic Clothing Tool directly.  
You need to match the 3D model with the costume first.  
In the menu bar, find Virtual Model and select Virtual Model Editor.  
At the top of the Virtual Model Editor, find Costume Fitting.  
There are two ways to create a costume.  
First, you can try the Automatic Clothing Tool.  
In the upper right corner, click the Automatic Clothing Tool button.  
You can see a gray shadow version around the model.  
Click the Automatic Clothing Tool button at the bottom.  
Rotate to see if the red costume fitting around the model is smooth.  
In this way, the costume fitting of the model is completed.  
If the costume fitting is not created correctly,  
then you need to use manual creation.  
You need to draw a line on the model according to the mouse instructions.  
First, draw a neckline.  
Draw three dots on the neck.  
Next is the neckline.  
It uses the same creation method.  
Follow the same method to complete the rest of the parts.  
Click the  
Automatically Create Costume Fitting button at the bottom of the list.  
Click the button below the list to create the costume fitting.  
You can complete the manual creation of the costume fitting.  
After the creation is completed, click Save.  
You can save the model with the costume fitting.  

Now let's see how to replace the model.  
Open the model directly.  
You can use the switch to switch the model.  
In the 3D toolbar, click on Automatic Clothing.  
Now this model has been replaced.  
In the 3D toolbar, click on Automatic Clothing.  
Now this model has been replaced.  
In the 3D toolbar, click on Automatic Clothing.  
Click on Automatic Clothing.

chunks.title: CLO Tips Classroom - Automatic Dressing Tool
chunks.content: # CLO Tips Classroom - Automatic Dressing Tool This document explains how to use the **Automatic Clothing Tool** in CLO for fitting costumes on virtual 3D models, including handling default CLO models and external models. It covers procedures for automatic and manual costume fitting, model size adjustments, pose checking, and model replacement. --- ## Automatic Dressing with Default CLO Models This section describes how to use the Automatic Clothing Tool to quickly fit costumes on CLO's default 3D models by matching costume size and pose. - Open the project file containing the costume and default CLO 3D model. - In the **Object Window**, select the 3D model that corresponds to the desired size. - Click the **Automatic Clothing Tool** button in the 3D toolbar. - The costume automatically fits the model size very quickly. - Repeat this process for other poses by switching to the corresponding model and clicking the Automatic Clothing Tool again. - This workflow efficiently produces costume fittings for multiple sizes and poses. ### Checking Pose and Fit - To review fitting results across sizes and poses, go to the **Menu Bar** → **Production** → **Check Pose**. - This view displays the fitting effect of each size on a single page for easy comparison and quality control. --- ## Using the Automatic Clothing Tool with External Models External 3D models require additional preparation before using the Automatic Clothing Tool directly. This section explains how to create and apply costume fitting for external models. ### Preparing External Models for Costume Fitting 1. Open the external model in CLO. 2. Go to the **Menu Bar** → **Virtual Model** → **Virtual Model Editor**. 3. At the top of the editor, select **Costume Fitting**. ### Automatic Costume Fitting Attempt - Click the **Automatic Clothing Tool** button at the upper right. - A gray shadow outline appears around the model indicating the fitting area. - Click the Automatic Clothing Tool button at the bottom of the editor. - Rotate the model to verify if the red costume fitting conforms smoothly around the model. - If fitting is successful, the costume fitting process is complete. ### Manual Costume Fitting Creation If automatic fitting fails, manual creation is required: - Follow mouse instructions to draw fitting lines on the model. - Begin by drawing three dots to mark the neckline. - Complete the neckline by connecting these dots. - Repeat the same method to define other necessary fitting parts on the model. - After drawing all required lines, click the **Automatically Create Costume Fitting** button at the bottom. - This generates the costume fitting manually. - Click **Save** to preserve the external model with the new costume fitting. --- ## Replacing and Dressing Models This section explains how to replace the model in the workspace and apply the Automatic Clothing Tool to fit the costume on the new model. - Open the model file. - Use the switch option to select or replace the model as needed.

For default models, size matching and pose adjustments are quick and straightforward. For external models, costume fitting requires either automatic application or manual line drawing in the Virtual Model Editor. The **Check Pose** feature allows users to verify fitting results across multiple sizes and poses, ensuring efficient and accurate costume production workflows.
